Cholamandlam General Insurance ... vs Smt. Snatosh Kunwar
on 4 December, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:35574

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

 On The 4 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 2796 of 2017
 Cholamandlam General Insurance Co.Ltd.
 Versus
 Smt. Snatosh Kunwar And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Pankaj Kumar Jain, learned counsel for the appella
 Company.
 Shri Nitin Singh Bhati, learned counsel for respondents

 At Indore

sentences.text:
Order
The appellant / Insurance Company has filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 20.07.2017 passed by learned Additional Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ujjain (M.P.) in Claim Case No.214/2016.

1.1 The Insurance Company has challenged the finding on the ground that the Claims Tribunal has incorrectly concluded that the deceased was crushed by the insured vehicle, whereas in fact he was the person driving the vehicle.
The Company has also challenged the quantum of compensation.
2. The facts relevant to the case are on 09.05.2016 at around 2:00 PM, Tejusingh was cultivating his agricultural fields with a tractor bearing Chasis number NHN-4700-MF-340536 and Engine No.77150.
While doing so, he operated the tractor in a rash and negligent manner, causing a collision with Shambhu Singh, as a result of which the tractor overturned and crushed Shambhu Singh beneath it.
He was rushed to the Civil Hospital, Tarana, where the doctor NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35574 2 MA-2796-2017 declared him dead.

2.1 An intimation of the incident was given by the hospital to Police Station Tarana vide Ex. P-10 pursuant to which an entry was made in the daily diary (Ex. P-6) recording that Shambhu Singh had died after being crushed under the tractor.

This intimation was thereafter forwarded by the SHO,
Tarana to the jurisdictional Police Station, Makdone vide Ex. P-5

; however, while sending the letter,
it was mentioned that Shambhu Singh had died while driving the tractor.
The Insurance Company relied on this discrepancy and challenged the Tribunal's award by contending that Ex. P-5 had not been properly considered.

sentences.text: The claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act before the Claims Tribunal by respondents No.1 to 4 stated that Tejusingh was driving the tractor and Shambhu Singh was standing at the boundary of the field.

This fact was proved by leading evidence of Santosh Kunwar (AW-1) and Mahendra Singh (AW-2)
and by exhibiting documents from the criminal case.
2.3 The Insurance Company mounted its challenge based on Ex. P-5.
In support of this, it examined Amolsingh (NAW-4), the Head Constable who conducted the investigation after receiving intimation Ex. P-5 from Police Station, Tarana.

3. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that Ex. P-5 was brought on record by the claimants themselves; therefore, the contents of the document become binding upon them and they cannot turn away from the fact that the said document states that the deceased himself was driving the vehicle.
He thus submits that the Claims Tribunal erred in not believing the same.
3.1 Apart from this, he has also argued that the quantum of compensation is excessive, as the income of the deceased has been assessed on the higher side.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35574 3 MA-2796-2017 4 .

Per contra , learned counsel for the respondents No.1 to 4 / claimants submit that Ex. P-5 is in fact based on Exs. P-6 and Ex. P-10, neither of which mentions that Shambhu Singh was driving the tractor.
They only record that he was crushed by the vehicle.
Thus, the intimation in Ex. P-5 was issued without any investigation or factual basis.

He submits that the hospital sent an intimation to the police station,
which was merely forwarded by that police station to the jurisdictional police station without any inquiry; therefore, the Tribunal, while considering the effect of this document in para 14, correctly discarded the contention of the Insurance Company.
Accordingly, he prays for dismissal of the appeal on this ground.
4.1 As regards quantum of compensation, he submits that Rs.5,000/- per month is in fact on the lower side, as the deceased was engaged in agricultural work.
He therefore submits that the compensation ought to be enhanced.

5. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
6.
From a perusal of Ex. P-5 in the light of intimations on which it is based, it appears that the same was sent by the SHO, Tarana to Police Station Makdone.
It further emerges that Exs. P-6 and P-10 on the basis of which the letter Ex. P-5 was issued are consistent with each other and do not support the contents of Ex. P- 7.
Exs. P-6 and P-10 indicate that the deceased was crushed beneath the tractor.

However, Ex. P-5,
which is based on this very intimation states that he was crushed while driving the tractor.
This intimation is contrary to the material on record.

2 8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Claims Tribunal has correctly considered this aspect in para 14 of the impugned award.

It is significant that Police Station Makdone after receiving Ex. P-5 entrusted the investigation to Head Constable Amolsingh (NAW-4), who NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35574 4 MA-2796-2017 was examined by the Insurance Company itself.
9. However, during his examination not a single question was put to the said witness by the counsel for the Insurance Company with respect to Ex. P-5.
As such, this Court does not find any reason to interfere with the conclusions drawn by the Claims Tribunal regarding the accident and the death of Shambhu Singh, who was crushed under the tractor.

10. As regards the quantum of compensation, considering the fact that the accident occurred on 19.05.2016 and that the Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased on a notional basis at Rs.5,000/- per month.
This Court is of the considered view that assessment is not on the higher side.
11. As such, the present appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Anushree Cholamandlam General Insurance ... vs Smt. Snatosh Kunwar on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196584633/
